recommended_pair.source: Supplied dwrap_index(1).xlsx; exact original values through tmp/extracted/workbook.json
rules: Show 0–1 ICW scores as published, or explicitly label multiplication by 100 as index points. They are not percentages of rights.
Excerpts illustrate part of the largest field difference. They do not reconstruct inverse-covariance weights or explain a percentage contribution.
The movement field also includes identity/travel documents. The excerpt comparison concerns settlement/free movement.
These are recorded 2022 dataset scores, not an assessment of current law or implementation.

codebook.source: DWRAP Technical Guide, September 2024; PDF pp13–14 (printed pp12–13)

move.0: No provision guaranteeing free movement within the host country

move_cond.0: No free-movement provision, OR government permission plus at least one other restriction
move_cond.1: Government permission OR one other restriction

camp.0: Designated areas exist and residence is required
camp.1: Designated areas exist; living outside allowed with government permission

codebook.warning: These are the codebook labels, not our independent certification that the laws have no exceptions. Both countries have camp=1. Code 0 is not by itself evidence of a prohibition.

evidence.quote: has the right to move freely in the country and choose his or her place of residence.
evidence.language: English; Ministry of the Interior translation from Finnish, legally binding only in Finnish and Swedish
evidence.original_language_excerpt: oikeus liikkua maassa ja valita asuinpaikkansa.
evidence.source_version: Amendments through 1163/2019; translation completed 26 May 2020. Section 41 wording also verified identical in translation through 389/2023, PDF p27. Section 41 is unmarked as amended in both consolidations. This is a historical provision check, not certification of every provision of the 2022 framework.
evidence.context: The quoted subject is an alien residing legally in Finland. Section 40(3) includes the period while an application is processed until a final decision or an enforceable removal decision.
evidence.connection: The explicit general free-movement guarantee is consistent with the presence-of-guarantee distinction in move (Finland=2, Namibia=0).
evidence.visible_caveat: A general right is not the whole law: section 120a also permits individual reception-centre residence/reporting orders for applicants under precautionary-measure conditions.
cannot_support: Do not claim every asylum seeker can always move without restriction.
Do not claim this quote independently validates Finland move_cond=2.
Do not infer camp differences: camp=1 in both countries.

evidence.document: Namibia Refugees (Recognition and Control) Act 2 of 1999
evidence.quote: without the prior written permission … leaves or attempts to leave such reception area or refugee settlement
evidence.language: English; original statutory language. Ellipsis removes intervening identification of the responsible officer and the required residence.
evidence.source_version: Legislation as at 19 March 1999, in Laws.Africa reproduction checked through 19 January 2024. No amendment annotation on sections 20–21. Matches original Gazette text indexed from Namibian ministry copy.
evidence.context: Section 20 permits written residence orders for recognized refugees, protected persons, asylum applicants, and specified family members. Section 21 applies to a person duly served with such an order; leaving or attempting to leave without prior written permission is an offence, punishable on conviction by up to 90 days imprisonment.
evidence.connection: The statute supplies positive evidence of a permission requirement for people under residence orders. We do not infer a ban merely from Namibia move=0.
evidence.visible_caveat: This restriction applies to people served with a section 20 residence order; it is not a claim that every refugee is always confined.
cannot_support: Do not equate move=0 with a total statutory ban on movement.
Do not claim all recognized refugees necessarily receive a residence order.
Do not claim the excerpt accounts for the full movement-field gap.

philippines_2022_audit_case.quote: Improve access of POCs to courts, documentation, health and welfare assistance, primary education, skills training and livelihood programs;
philippines_2022_audit_case.effectivity: Section 12: on publication in the Official Gazette or a newspaper of general circulation; do not assert an exact earliest effective date without checking newspaper publication.
philippines_2022_audit_case.dataset_issue: Supplied Philippines 2022 policy-title field names only Department Circular 058 (2012), twice concatenated. health=0, services_icw=0.0292850512 in clean export. EO163 is not named. Its preamble also records an inter-agency agreement dated 12 October 2017 for protection services.
philippines_2022_audit_case.interpretation: The 2022 EO is evidence that the dataset label and low services score cannot be read as a complete account of available protections in 2022. The order directs institutions to improve access; it does not itself quantify implementation or guarantee identical access to every service. The basis for its absence in DWRAP needs curator clarification.
do_not: Do not state Philippines provided no healthcare in 2022.
Do not silently replace or recalculate official scores.
Do not claim the EO necessarily establishes an unconditional individual right to all services.
Do not attribute the whole Austria–Philippines services gap to omission of this order.

chad_audit_leads_not_for_default.document: Loi No.027/PR/2020 Portant Asile en République du Tchad, 31 December 2020

items.observation: Explicit exemption from penal sanctions for irregular entry/stay, subject to direct arrival, presentation within 90 days, and valid reasons. Codebook 0=no exemption, 1=conditional exemption. Possible coding/scope discrepancy; do not silently recode.
The list of rights for refugees/asylum seekers with a provisional document includes the right to health. Possible coding/scope discrepancy.
Provides court access and same treatment as nationals regarding legal assistance. Whether this meets code2 needs coder clarification.
